nodes.label: MIRC Prototype Flow Guide
nodes.rationale: Plain-language walkthrough for panelists, advisers and organizers; describes the MIRC 2026 screens and has not been updated for the multi-conference Conference box.

nodes.label: Evidence Labels (CONFIRMED / ASSUMPTION / RECOMMENDATION / UNRESOLVED / EXACT / ESTIMATE)
nodes.norm_label: evidence labels (confirmed / assumption / recommendation / unresolved / exact / estimate)
nodes.rationale: Separates observed facts from working guesses and proposals so planning can continue without presenting guesses as requirements.

nodes.label: Grouped Navigation (Programme / About + Register and Submit buttons)
nodes.norm_label: grouped navigation (programme / about + register and submit buttons)
nodes.rationale: A flat 12-item menu is long for a phone, so pages are grouped with Register and Submit always visible.

nodes.label: Per-Edition Logo Record (prototype v4)
nodes.rationale: conference.logo_url is too thin for per-edition branding; a separate record with conference id in the file path stops one edition overwriting another's logo.

nodes.label: v1 Shared Status Query Service Design Note
nodes.norm_label: v1 shared status query service design note
nodes.rationale: Status filter doubles as mailing recipient group and book criterion, so one status query should feed all three.

nodes.label: Creating and publishing an edition (yearly flow)
nodes.norm_label: creating and publishing an edition (yearly flow)

nodes.label: customConferences localStorage
nodes.rationale: No server, so browser storage meets 'not lost on reload'; only the definition is saved, damaged entries are skipped one by one so a bad entry cannot stop the site opening.

nodes.label: Yearly edition rollover (P.newEdition)
nodes.rationale: Copies set-up (pages, rooms, topics, templates, settings) but never papers, people, schedule or news; resets dates so each year starts clean.

nodes.label: One site, many conferences, many years
nodes.norm_label: one site, many conferences, many years
nodes.rationale: No conference name or year is written into code: per-conference defaults live in conferences.js, per-year data in an edition record, screens ask P.tag()/P.series().code, so a new year or conference needs no code change.

nodes.label: Items for confirmation
nodes.rationale: Points not stated in the project files are marked 'to be confirmed' rather than guessed.

nodes.label: Blueprint roles (Guest to Administrator)
nodes.rationale: Eight roles from the blueprint; page read rights are set per page under Website > Pages and menu, not fixed per role.

nodes.label: My Account button
nodes.rationale: Replaced 'My Space (Participant)': covers registration, submissions, account details and sign-out; 'Participant Portal/Dashboard' rejected because reviewers and organizers use it too; role moved into the menu's first line.

nodes.label: Viewing as (role simulation)
nodes.rationale: Stands in for real sign-in, which needs an authentication service the prototype does not have.

nodes.label: Submission Statuses (Initial, Reviewed, Awaiting update, Accepted, Refused, No review)
nodes.norm_label: submission statuses (initial, reviewed, awaiting update, accepted, refused, no review)

nodes.label: User Roles (Guest, Member, Participant, Reviewer, Redactor, Webmaster, Administrator, Coordinator)
nodes.norm_label: user roles (guest, member, participant, reviewer, redactor, webmaster, administrator, coordinator)

nodes.label: Website Module (General, Header, Appearance, Pages, Homepage, News, Uploads, Statistics)
nodes.norm_label: website module (general, header, appearance, pages, homepage, news, uploads, statistics)

nodes.label: Per-Page Rights (Right to consult / Right to edit)
nodes.norm_label: per-page rights (right to consult / right to edit)
nodes.rationale: Role rights belong on the page, not only on the user; the live site's Pages module sets read and edit roles per page.

nodes.label: Shared Status Query Service
nodes.rationale: The status filter also acts as a mailing recipient group and a book-of-abstracts criterion, so one status query service should feed all three.

nodes.label: Calendar date picker and 24-hour time boxes
nodes.norm_label: calendar date picker and 24-hour time boxes

nodes.label: Visitor-site colors (8-color palette)
nodes.rationale: Palette written as --t-* variables on the .site wrapper and re-pointed in styles.css so every component follows it with no colors in components; admin area stays outside .site and keeps its own colors.

nodes.label: Classic scripts, not ES modules
nodes.rationale: Browsers block modules when a page is opened straight from a folder (file://), so plain scripts loaded in a fixed order are used.

nodes.label: Plain HTML/CSS/JS with no build step
nodes.norm_label: plain html/css/js with no build step
nodes.rationale: Blueprint's Next.js, Tailwind and Supabase need a build and a server, making the prototype harder to open and test; styles.css tokens reuse the blueprint's Tailwind token names so they carry over.

nodes.label: Design for older administrators
nodes.rationale: Most administrators are older adults: large relative-sized text, plain words, big targets, confirmation with safe default, words plus symbols never color alone, persistent messages, keyboard focus ring.

nodes.label: MIRC Color Palette Tokens (slate-green, forest, leaf, navy, deep-green, gold-*)
nodes.norm_label: mirc color palette tokens (slate-green, forest, leaf, navy, deep-green, gold-*)

nodes.label: D6: Brand Details Not in Images
nodes.norm_label: d6: brand details not in images

nodes.label: Next.js (App Router)
nodes.rationale: Server-rendered pages for search engines plus server actions in the same repo, so there is one thing to deploy.

nodes.label: Recommended Technology Stack (section 12.2)
nodes.rationale: Small scale (253 registrations, 214 submissions) needs no clusters or microservices; one TypeScript repository with SSR pages and a relational database fits.

nodes.label: Four Uploaded Reference Images (certificate, two title slides, Opening Remarks card)
nodes.norm_label: four uploaded reference images (certificate, two title slides, opening remarks card)

nodes.label: Visitor-Site Palette Settings (Website > Site colors, prototype v5)
nodes.norm_label: visitor-site palette settings (website > site colors, prototype v5)
nodes.rationale: Each edition changes its own copy of the default palette for the public site only; derived colors are computed, never entered, and a failing palette needs explicit confirmation to save.

nodes.label: Supabase (Postgres, Auth, Storage)
nodes.rationale: Database, auth and storage in one vendor with Row Level Security to enforce roles inside the database.

nodes.label: Vercel Hosting
nodes.rationale: Verified Next.js adapter; Pro recommended for production because Hobby is restricted to non-commercial personal use.

nodes.label: Accessibility Target WCAG 2.2 AA
nodes.rationale: The live Sciencesconf footer states 'Accessibility: non-compliant', so the rebuild has room to do better.

nodes.label: Light Mode Only Decision
nodes.rationale: The images show light backgrounds only and dark mode is not a stated requirement, so building it now adds cost without a confirmed benefit.

nodes.label: Save as draft / Publish now pattern
nodes.norm_label: save as draft / publish now pattern
nodes.rationale: On a published edition visitors keep the old logo/colors while Webmaster and Administrator preview the draft, which can then be published or discarded.

nodes.label: Logo upload specification
nodes.rationale: Minimum 240 px = 2x the 120 px header frame for high-res screens; 600x600 recommended to stay sharp at Largest on the home page; rounded square frame holds square, round and wide logos; type checked by first bytes, SVG only shown via img so it cannot run code.
